take: Oil fell on renewed hope for a US/Iran truce that would supposedly reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week, a headline risk that matters far more than any single inventory print because it threatens to normalise the geopolitical premium baked into crude and, by extension, product cracks. On the freight side, Houston has seen a drop in bunker operations for crude tankers this month per Spotbarge, whilst Sincere Navigation paid $38.5m for a 2019-built kamsarmax and Rio Tinto offloaded its final two newcastlemaxes to Yasa, a reminder that dry bulk asset rotation continues even as tanker bunkering activity cools. The flow angle is the EIA's forecast of record US crude production at 13.8m b/d in 2026, surpassing 2025's 13.7m b/d, which keeps barrels long and caps rallies unless the Hormuz story escalates. Cross-market, the $14/mt spread between the best and worst Singapore bunker suppliers on cost of doing business is a direct margin tax on owners already squeezed by elevated crack spreads feeding into higher pump prices. Watch in the next 24 hours whether the Iran truce rhetoric hardens into anything concrete on Hormuz transit, and whether Singapore bunker premiums widen further as suppliers reprice that $14/mt dispersion.

items.title: Henry Hub natural gas prices this summer were 6% lower than last summer
items.summary: The Henry Hub natural gas spot price averaged $2.93 per million British thermal units from June through August, 6% less than the same period last year. Prices were lower this summer despite exceptionally hot weather that increased electricity demand for air conditioning. Natural gas-fired power plants often help meet higher demand during such periods.

items.title: Public companies produce most U.S. crude oil and natural gas
items.summary: Publicly traded companies represent a tiny share of the total number of companies producing crude oil and natural gas in the United States, but they make up a large share of U.S. production. In 2025, publicly traded companies accounted for just 2% of about 12,000 oil and natural gas producers but produced 68% of the crude oil and natural gas in the Lower 48 states.

items.title: What goes into diesel prices?
items.summary: The price of distillate fuel oil, often sold as diesel, is driven by the price of crude oil, retail margins, distribution costs, taxes, and crack spreads, the indicator we use for refining margins. Tight global supplies of distillate fuel oil and elevated crude oil prices have driven prices higher in recent months.
